meta.title: Dad’s Trip 2026/27
meta.about: Thirty-six nights: London with your daughter, eleven on the Hurtigruten chasing the northern lights, Christmas in London, Dublin for the Guinness, Arsenal on the 30th, and the last 115 km of the Camino into Santiago. Open Go to see only what is happening now. Everything still to decide is on Decisions, one question at a time.

days.title: Land in London
days.notes: Saturday, so she is not at work. Do nothing today except get to a bed.

items.title: Land at Heathrow
items.notes: Allow 45 to 90 minutes to get through the border and collect the bag. Then the Elizabeth line into central London, about 30 minutes, or the Heathrow Express if you are past caring. AGREE BEFORE YOU FLY exactly where you are meeting her: Heathrow has four terminals, they are miles apart, and the phone signal in the baggage hall is poor.

items.title: To your daughter’s
items.notes: Eat whatever she puts in front of you and go to bed early. You will wake at 3am regardless; that is normal and it passes in two days.

days.title: London, no plans
days.notes: Sunday with her. A roast if she is up for it.

days.title: London, your own time
days.notes: She is back at work. Three quiet days before the ship: this is deliberate, not a gap to fill. The Imperial War Museum is the one to do if you do one thing.

items.title: Imperial War Museum
items.notes: Free. The best war museum in the country and the one that will hold you longest: the First World War galleries, the Second World War and Holocaust galleries, and the atrium full of aircraft. Give it three hours. Nearest tube Lambeth North or Elephant & Castle.

days.title: London, your own time
days.notes: Nothing booked. Churchill War Rooms if you want a second war day.

items.title: Churchill War Rooms
items.location: Clive Steps, King Charles St, London SW1A 2AQ
items.notes: The underground bunker Churchill ran the war from, left as it was in 1945. About £32 and you must book a time slot online, it sells out. Two hours. Right by St James’s Park.

days.title: London, and pack for Norway
days.notes: Pack tonight, not tomorrow morning. Norway in December is dark, wet and about freezing: thermals, a proper waterproof, a warm hat, gloves, and boots with grip.

days.title: Fly to Bergen
days.notes: A day early on purpose. The ship sails tomorrow evening and you do not fly to a cruise on the day it leaves.

items.title: Norwegian, Gatwick to Bergen
items.notes: Norwegian is the only airline flying this nonstop, about 1h55, and it runs most days. The 08:40 arriving 11:35 is the good one. GATWICK, NOT HEATHROW: allow 90 minutes from central London on the Gatwick Express from Victoria, and leave her place by about 05:30. Book this as soon as the dates are certain; December fares only go up.

items.title: Airport to the city
items.notes: The Bybanen light rail runs from outside the terminal to the city centre in about 45 minutes and costs a fraction of a taxi. Buy the ticket from the machine on the platform.

items.title: Check in, Bergen
items.notes: Dark by about 15:30 this far north in December. Do not fight it. Get warm, eat early, sleep.

days.title: A day in Bergen, then the ship
days.notes: THE DAY YOU ASKED FOR. The ship does not sail until 20:30, so you have the whole of Bergen with a bag already in a hotel. Daylight is roughly 09:30 to 15:30, so front-load it.

items.title: Bryggen, the old wharf
items.notes: The row of crooked wooden merchant houses on the harbour, UNESCO listed, and the reason people photograph Bergen. Wander the alleys behind the front row. Free, and 10 minutes from the fish market.

items.title: Fish market, then something hot
items.notes: The indoor market is open year round. Fish soup or a prawn sandwich. BE READY FOR NORWEGIAN PRICES: a pint is about A$16 and a modest lunch A$35. This is the single most expensive country on the trip and you are only here two days, so eat what you want and stop converting.

items.title: Fløibanen funicular up Mount Fløyen
items.notes: Eight minutes up, and the view back over the city and the fjord is the one to send home. Go before the light goes. Cafe at the top if it is foul.

items.title: Collect the bag, get to the terminal
items.notes: About 20 minutes on foot from the centre, or a short taxi with the case. Hurtigruten asks you to be in the terminal no later than 30 minutes before departure, so be there by 19:30 at the very latest. Being there at 18:00 with a book is a better evening than cutting it fine.

items.title: Hurtigruten sails for Kirkenes
items.notes: CHECK YOUR PAPERWORK ON THIS ONE. You told Connor 09:30, but Hurtigruten has sailed from Bergen at 20:30 for years and the 14:45 you gave for the return is exactly right, which says the booking is the classic 12-day round voyage. If it really is 09:30 the whole of this day changes, so read the confirmation and tell him. If it is 20:30, today is a free day in Bergen you did not know you had.

days.title: At sea, heading north
days.notes: Somewhere around here you cross the Arctic Circle. They make a thing of it.

days.title: Tromsø and the lights country
days.notes: The middle of the voyage is the best of the northern lights window. Dress for standing still outside in the cold, which is much colder than walking in it.

days.title: Kirkenes, then turn south
days.notes: The turning point. From here you see by day the ports you passed in the dark.

days.title: Southbound, last full day
days.notes: Pack tonight.

days.title: Back in Bergen
days.notes: Off the ship at 14:45 and STAYING IN BERGEN TONIGHT. You could chase an evening flight to London but it is two days before Christmas, the airports are at their worst, and if it goes wrong you are stranded on the 23rd. One calm night is worth the hotel.

items.title: Hurtigruten docks in Bergen
items.notes: Eleven nights done.

items.title: One night in Bergen
items.notes: Same hotel as the 10th if they have it; you will know the way.

days.title: Bergen to London
days.notes: Home to her place, with Christmas Eve clear.

items.title: Norwegian, Bergen to Gatwick
items.notes: Book this at the same time as the outbound. Whatever you do, do not take the last flight of the day on the 23rd of December.

days.title: Christmas Eve
days.notes: With her. Nothing planned.

days.title: Christmas Day
days.notes: The fixed point of the whole trip.

items.title: Christmas with your daughter
items.notes: ONE THING TO KNOW: London transport STOPS on Christmas Day. Not reduced, stopped. No tube, no buses, no trains. If you are not already where you need to be by Christmas Eve night you are walking or paying a fortune for a taxi, if you can find one.

days.title: Boxing Day
days.notes: Quiet. Pack a small bag for Dublin.

days.title: Fly to Dublin
days.notes: THE IRELAND WINDOW. Two nights between Christmas and the football, which is the only gap on the whole trip that fits it. Take hand luggage only.

items.title: London to Dublin
items.location: Heathrow, Gatwick, Stansted or Luton to Dublin
items.notes: About 1h25 and they go all day from every London airport. Aer Lingus and Ryanair both. Book when the dates are settled. Ireland is not in the UK, so you clear passport control, but Australians need nothing beyond the passport.

items.title: Check in, Dublin
items.notes: Stay near the centre, around Temple Bar or Grafton Street, so everything is walkable and you are not learning a bus network for two nights.

days.title: Guinness, and then better Guinness
days.notes: The one day you came for.

items.title: Guinness Storehouse
items.notes: Seven floors about how it is made, ending at the Gravity Bar on the roof with a 360-degree view over Dublin and a pint included in the ticket. BOOK ONLINE AND IN ADVANCE, it is the most visited thing in Ireland and it sells out. About €30. Two hours is enough.

items.title: The real pint: the Long Hall, Kehoe’s or the Palace Bar
items.location: South Great George’s St, South Anne St, Fleet St
items.notes: This is the actual point. The Storehouse is the tour; these are the pubs. Victorian interiors, no televisions, and a barman who pours it in two goes and lets it settle. Ask for a pint of Guinness and then leave it alone for two minutes. Also worth it: EPIC, the Irish emigration museum at the docks, which is genuinely good and half an hour away on foot.

items.title: Dinner, and a session if you find one
items.location: Around Temple Bar, but not in it
items.notes: Temple Bar itself is a tourist trap and charges double. Walk two streets out. Irish stew, or seafood chowder with brown bread. Live traditional music happens most nights around Christmas; ask the barman where, not the internet.

days.title: Dublin to London
days.notes: Back today, not tomorrow. The football is tomorrow and you are not leaving it to a morning flight.

items.title: Dublin to London
items.notes: An afternoon or early evening flight. Keeps the whole of tomorrow clear.

days.title: Arsenal v Fulham
days.notes: Emirates Stadium. A London derby, and the ground is one of the best in the country.

items.title: Arsenal v Fulham, Emirates Stadium
items.location: Emirates Stadium, Hornsey Rd, London N7 7AJ
items.notes: CHECK THE KICK-OFF TIME AGAIN IN DECEMBER. Premier League fixtures get moved for television, sometimes by a day, and the broadcast picks for this round are usually confirmed about six weeks out. Holloway Road on the Piccadilly line is the nearest tube and it is mobbed afterwards; Arsenal or Finsbury Park are a slightly longer walk and much easier. Go early, the ground is worth seeing filling up. It is cold: more layers than you think.

days.title: New Year’s Eve
days.notes: Whatever she is doing. The fireworks on the Thames need a ticket months ahead, so watch them on television like most of London does.

days.title: New Year’s Day
days.notes: Rest. Pack for Spain: you are walking 115 km in six days starting the day after tomorrow.

days.title: Fly to Spain, and get to Sarria
days.notes: A long travel day, and the only one on the Camino leg. Everything after this is walking.

items.title: Ryanair, Stansted to Santiago de Compostela
items.location: London Stansted to Santiago de Compostela
items.notes: Ryanair is the only nonstop and IT ONLY FLIES MONDAY, WEDNESDAY AND SATURDAY. That is why today is a Saturday and why you come home on Saturday the 9th. About 2h10. Stansted is an early start from London, so consider a hotel at the airport the night before. Hand luggage only if you can: you are carrying this for six days.

items.title: Santiago to Sarria
items.notes: About 2.5 hours by train or bus. Yes, you travel to the far end and walk back; that is how the last 100 km works. Book the train on Renfe when the date is close.

items.title: First night in Sarria
items.notes: GET YOUR CREDENCIAL TONIGHT if you have not already: the pilgrim passport you collect stamps in. The parish church and most pilgrim hostels in Sarria issue them for a couple of euros. Without it there is no Compostela at the other end.

days.title: Sarria to Portomarín, 22 km
days.notes: Day one. Rolling farmland, oak woods and stone hamlets. Light from about 08:45 to 18:15, so leave by 09:00 and you have hours in hand.

items.title: Walk Sarria to Portomarín
items.notes: 22 km, five to six hours at a steady pace with stops. The 100 km marker is just outside Sarria and everybody photographs it. TWO STAMPS A DAY from here on, from bars, churches or hostels, because the last 100 km has the stricter rule. Portomarín is reached over a long bridge and up a staircase, which is a cruel finish, and the village was moved stone by stone when they dammed the river.

days.title: Portomarín to Palas de Rei, 25 km
days.notes: The longest day of the six. Start early.

items.title: Walk Portomarín to Palas de Rei
items.notes: 25 km with a long steady climb out of Portomarín in the first two hours. Get it done in the morning. There are bars at Gonzar and Ventas de Narón for coffee and a stamp.

days.title: Palas de Rei to Melide, 15 km
days.notes: A short day on purpose, after the long one.

items.title: Walk Palas de Rei to Melide
items.notes: 15 km, three to four hours. Melide is the octopus town: Pulpería Ezéquiel is the famous one and pulpo a feira, octopus with paprika, olive oil and coarse salt on a wooden plate, is what you eat there. Earned it.

days.title: Melide to Arzúa, 14 km
days.notes: The shortest day, and a Spanish public holiday.

items.title: Walk Melide to Arzúa
items.notes: 14 km through eucalyptus woods. TODAY IS DÍA DE REYES, Epiphany, and it is a bigger day in Spain than Christmas: shops shut, some bars shut, and there are parades the evening before. The walking is unaffected but buy anything you need the day before. Arzúa is the cheese town, a soft cow’s cheese called tetilla.

days.title: Arzúa to O Pedrouzo, 20 km
days.notes: Last full day before Santiago.

items.title: Walk Arzúa to O Pedrouzo
items.notes: 20 km, gentle. You start meeting people who are also finishing tomorrow.

days.title: O Pedrouzo to Santiago, 20 km. You arrive
days.notes: The last day. Leave in the dark if you want to reach the cathedral by lunchtime.

items.title: Walk O Pedrouzo into Santiago
items.notes: 20 km. Past the airport, over Monte do Gozo where pilgrims first see the spires, then down into the old city and under the archway into Praça do Obradoiro with the cathedral in front of you. 115 km on foot. Take your time on the last hour.

items.title: Collect your Compostela at the Pilgrim’s Office
items.location: Oficina del Peregrino, Rúa das Carretas 33
items.notes: Bring the credencial with its two stamps a day. They check it, ask why you walked, and write your name on the certificate in Latin. Free. There is a queue; in January it will be short. THE PILGRIM MASS at the cathedral is usually at noon and again at 19:30, and the botafumeiro, the giant swinging incense burner, is not swung at every mass, so ask at the office which one to go to.

items.title: Dinner on Rúa do Franco
items.location: Rúa do Franco, behind the cathedral
items.notes: The street of restaurants. Octopus, pimientos de Padrón, scallops, and Estrella Galicia, which is the local beer and very good. This is the meal at the end of the walk, so have the good one.

days.title: Santiago to London
days.notes: Fly back today. Stansted, then across London.

items.title: Ryanair, Santiago to Stansted
items.notes: Saturday is one of the three days it flies. CONFIRM THE RETURN DAY when you book: the outbound runs Mon, Wed and Sat and the return usually matches, but check before you commit to the 9th. Stansted to central London is the Stansted Express, about 50 minutes.

items.title: Last night in London
items.location: Her place, or a hotel near Heathrow
items.notes: A HEATHROW HOTEL IS WORTH IT TONIGHT if she does not live west. Tomorrow is a 13:40 flight, you will be tired from a week of walking, and crossing London with a case on a Sunday morning with engineering works is a poor way to end five weeks.

days.title: Fly home
days.notes: Thirty-six nights. Home tomorrow.

items.title: To Heathrow
items.notes: Be at the airport by 10:40 for a 13:40 departure. A Sunday, so check the night before for engineering works on whichever line you are using.

items.title: Heathrow to Brisbane
items.notes: CLAIM YOUR VAT REFUND BEFORE YOU DROP THE BAG if you bought anything substantial in Spain or Ireland. The UK no longer does tax-free shopping for visitors, but the EU does, so Spanish and Irish purchases over about €100 qualify and the refund desk is landside.

stays.name: Your daughter’s place
stays.notes: Which nights is Decisions question 2. Once you know, put the number in here and the budget sorts itself out.

stays.name: London hotel nights
stays.notes: Placeholder for whatever is not at hers. Book in November.

stays.name: Bergen, night of 10 Dec
stays.distance: Walkable to Bryggen and the Hurtigruten terminal
stays.notes: The night before the ship. Somewhere central so the whole of the 11th is on foot.

stays.name: Bergen, night of 22 Dec
stays.notes: Off the ship at 14:45 and fly to London tomorrow. Same hotel as the 10th if they have it.

stays.name: Dublin, 27 to 29 Dec
stays.notes: Near Grafton Street or the south quays. Walkable to everything, including the Storehouse at a push.

stays.name: Palas de Rei, night of 4 Jan
Santiago de Compostela, night of 8 Jan
stays.notes: The night you arrive. Somewhere in the old town, within sight of the cathedral if you can.

stays.name: Stansted airport hotel, night of 1 Jan
stays.notes: A 07:40 flight out of Stansted on New Year’s Day morning is not a thing to attempt from central London.

food.dish: Guinness at the Storehouse, then the real one in a pub
food.where: Storehouse at St James’s Gate; then the Long Hall, Kehoe’s or the Palace Bar
food.why: The Storehouse is the tour and the rooftop view, with a pint in the ticket. The actual best pint in Dublin is in a Victorian pub with no television, poured in two goes and left to settle. Do both, in that order.

food.dish: Seafood chowder and brown bread, or a proper Irish stew
food.where: Anywhere two streets away from Temple Bar
food.why: Temple Bar charges double for worse. Walk out of it.

food.where: Any pub with a blackboard and no television
food.why: Beef, Yorkshire pudding, gravy. Book it; the good ones fill by Thursday.

food.dish: Fish soup at the Torget market
food.where: Torget fish market, indoor hall, open year round
food.why: The thing to eat in Bergen, and it is hot, which matters in December.

food.dish: Pulpo a feira at Pulpería Ezéquiel
food.where: Melide, on the Camino, day four
food.why: Octopus with paprika, olive oil and coarse salt on a wooden plate. Melide is where pilgrims stop for it and Ezéquiel is the one they stop at. You will have walked 15 km to get there.
The soft cow’s cheese the town is known for. Buy a piece for the next day’s walk.

food.dish: Scallops, Padrón peppers, and Estrella Galicia
food.where: Rúa do Franco, the restaurant street behind the cathedral
food.why: The meal at the end of the walk. The scallop shell is the symbol of the Camino, so eating one here is the joke everybody makes and it is still good. Estrella Galicia is the local beer and better than its reputation.

food.where: Any bar with a board outside at lunchtime
food.why: Three courses, bread and a glass of wine for about €12 to €15, served between about 13:30 and 15:30. It is how Spain eats lunch and it is the best value on this trip by a mile.

budget.label: Food and drink in the UK and Ireland, about 21 days
budget.notes: About A$90 a day eating reasonably and having a few pints. Less on the days your daughter cooks. The named meals in Dublin and Santiago are already on the itinerary and are not in this number.

budget.label: Food and drink in Spain, 8 days
budget.notes: About A$65 a day, and Galicia is good value. The menu del dia is three courses, bread and a glass of wine for 12 to 15 euro at lunchtime, which is how to eat on a walking day.

budget.label: Eating ashore in Norway, 2 days
budget.notes: Meals on the ship are included, so this is only the two days in Bergen, where a pint is about A$16 and a modest lunch A$35.

budget.label: Tubes, buses, airport trains, an Oyster card
budget.notes: The Gatwick and Stansted Express runs, getting about London for five weeks, and the Bybanen in Bergen. The Santiago to Sarria train is on the itinerary.

budget.label: Travel insurance, 37 days, age 63, with cruise cover
budget.notes: Shop around, but do not buy the cheapest without reading what it says about cruises. Cruise cover is nearly always a separate tick box.

budget.label: UK ETA, ETIAS and an eSIM
Camino luggage transfer, 6 stages
budget.notes: About 8 euro a stage for a van to take the bag on to the next guesthouse. Optional, and see Decisions, but it is the difference between walking with 3 kg and 8 kg.

budget.label: Contingency
budget.notes: Five weeks. Something always comes up: a taxi you did not plan, a jumper you did not pack, a round you insist on buying.

checklist.text: Apply for the UK ETA. You cannot board without it
checklist.notes: Since 25 February 2026 every Australian passport holder needs an Electronic Travel Authorisation to enter the UK. £20, on the official UK ETA app or at gov.uk, usually approved in minutes though they ask you to allow three working days. Lasts two years. THE AIRLINE CHECKS IT AT THE GATE IN BRISBANE: no ETA, no boarding, no refund. Use gov.uk and nothing else, because the copycat sites charge four times the price for the same thing.

checklist.text: Check the passport: 6 months left AND issued within the last 10 years
checklist.notes: Two separate rules and the second one catches people. Norway and Spain are both Schengen, which requires the passport to be valid at least 3 months after you leave AND to have been issued within the last 10 years. An Australian passport renewed early carries extra months that can push its issue date past ten years, and that passport gets refused while looking perfectly in date. Check the ISSUE date. Renewal takes about six weeks and longer near Christmas.

checklist.text: Watch for ETIAS opening, then apply. Norway and Spain both need it
checklist.notes: ETIAS is the European travel permit Australians will need for the Schengen countries. This trip enters Schengen twice, Norway on the 10th of December and Spain on the 2nd of January. Expected to start in the last months of 2026 with a grace period into 2027, so your dates may fall either side. About €20. THE SITE IS NOT OPEN YET AND EVERY WEBSITE CURRENTLY TAKING ETIAS APPLICATIONS IS A SCAM. Wait. Connor is checking the real date in November.

checklist.text: Travel insurance: 37 days, age 63, must include the cruise
checklist.notes: Cruise cover is nearly always a separate tick box and a policy without it pays for nothing that happens on the ship. Declare every medical condition honestly; an undeclared one voids the whole policy. Also worth knowing: Australia has reciprocal healthcare agreements with the UK, Ireland and Norway, so medically necessary treatment is covered there on your Medicare card. That is real but it is NOT insurance. It does not fly you home and it does not cover Spain.

checklist.text: Gatwick to Bergen on 10 Dec, and Bergen to Gatwick on 23 Dec
checklist.notes: Norwegian is the only nonstop, about 1h55. The 08:40 out of Gatwick arriving 11:35 is the one. Going on the 10th rather than the 11th is deliberate: you never fly to a cruise on the day it sails. Coming back on the 23rd rather than the evening of the 22nd is the same logic in reverse, two days before Christmas.

checklist.text: Two nights in Bergen: 10 Dec and 22 Dec
checklist.notes: Same hotel both times if you can. Bergen is expensive, about A$250 a night, and the centre is small enough that anything near Bryggen or the fish market is walkable to the Hurtigruten terminal.
Ireland’s most visited attraction and it sells out, especially in the week between Christmas and New Year. Book a morning slot online, about €30, which includes the pint at the top.

checklist.text: Dublin flights and two nights, 27 to 29 Dec
checklist.notes: About 1h25, they go all day from every London airport. Stay near Grafton Street or the south side of the river so everything is walkable.

checklist.text: Stansted to Santiago on Sat 2 Jan, back Sat 9 Jan
checklist.notes: Ryanair is the only nonstop and IT ONLY FLIES MONDAY, WEDNESDAY AND SATURDAY, which is what fixes the Camino dates. Confirm the return runs on the Saturday before you commit. Book the Stansted airport hotel for the night of the 1st at the same time.

checklist.text: Seven nights on the Camino: Sarria, Portomarín, Palas de Rei, Melide, Arzúa, O Pedrouzo, Santiago
checklist.notes: BOOK THESE AHEAD, do not walk in. Most pilgrim albergues close from Christmas to mid-January, so this is a hotel and guesthouse walk rather than a hostel one. That costs more, about A$120 a night, and at 63 with a private room and a hot shower every night it is the better trip anyway. Somewhere with a drying room is worth paying for in Galician January.

checklist.text: Decide the London hotel nights and book them
checklist.notes: You are at your daughter’s for some of it and in a hotel for the rest. Work out which nights with her BEFORE you book anything: five weeks is a long time to have a guest and she may be relieved to be asked. Whatever is left is the biggest single cost in the trip.

checklist.text: Break the boots in now. Not in December, now
checklist.notes: Six days and 115 km. Walk 10 km in them, then 15, then 20, on hills, in the rain, with the pack you will carry. Blisters on day two of six is the one thing that can actually ruin this, and it is entirely preventable. If the boots hurt at all in Gympie they will be agony in Galicia.

checklist.text: Get a credencial, the pilgrim passport
checklist.notes: You collect stamps in it and hand it in at Santiago to get the Compostela. Buy it in Sarria for a couple of euros at the parish church or a hostel, or order one from the Australian Friends of the Camino before you leave. ON THE LAST 100 KM THE RULE IS TWO STAMPS A DAY, not one: bars, cafes, churches and hostels all stamp. Miss the stamps and there is no certificate.

checklist.text: Pack for Galician rain, not Spanish sun
checklist.notes: January in Galicia is 5 to 12 degrees and it is the wettest part of Spain. A proper waterproof jacket, a pack cover, two pairs of walking socks so one can dry, and a head torch because it is not light until nearly 09:00. Keep the pack under 8 kg; every kilo is 115 km of carrying it. Luggage transfer between stages costs about €8 a day and is a perfectly respectable thing to use.

checklist.text: Put an eSIM on the iPhone before you leave
checklist.notes: One eSIM covering the UK and Europe is about A$25 for the month and saves both roaming charges and hunting for wi-fi. Install it at home where the internet is good and someone can help, then switch it on when you land. Keep the Australian number active for bank texts.

checklist.text: Two cards from two banks, in two different pockets
checklist.notes: A card that stops working in Norway on a Sunday is a ruined day if it is the only one you have. Tell both banks the dates. Ask what they charge on foreign purchases, because 3% is common and over 37 days it adds up to real money; a fee-free travel card is worth getting.

checklist.text: Ask Hurtigruten for the port-by-port timetable and send it to Connor
checklist.notes: Which port each day and what time the ship is alongside. Once that is in here you will always know what tomorrow is, which is the whole reason this is on your phone.

checklist.text: Ask Hurtigruten about the Northern Lights Promise
checklist.notes: Hurtigruten has long run a guarantee on the 12-day round voyage in the winter months: if the aurora does not appear, you get another voyage free. Terms change, so ask them directly whether your booking has it and what counts. Worth knowing before you go rather than after.

places.name: Emirates Stadium
places.notes: Arsenal. Holloway Road, Arsenal or Finsbury Park tube.

places.name: Hurtigruten terminal, Bergen
places.notes: Nøstegaten 30. In the terminal 30 min before sailing.

places.name: Pilgrim’s Office, Santiago
places.notes: Rúa das Carretas 33. Bring the credencial.

questions.question: Does the Hurtigruten booking really say 09:30?
questions.why: You told Connor the ship leaves at 09:30 on the 11th. Hurtigruten has sailed from Bergen at 20:30 for years, and the 14:45 you gave for the return is exactly their Bergen arrival time, which says this is the classic 12-day round voyage. If it is 20:30, you have a free day in Bergen. If it really is 09:30, the whole of the 10th and 11th changes.
options: Not sure, need to find the confirmation
questions.recommendation: Read the confirmation email and tell Connor. Everything about the 10th and 11th of December hangs on it.

questions.question: Which nights are you at your daughter’s and which need a hotel?
questions.why: It is the biggest number in the budget by a distance. Each night at hers saves about A$220, and ten hotel nights against five is a A$1,100 difference. It also needs asking rather than assuming: five weeks is a long time to have a guest, even your own father.
options: Mostly at hers, a hotel for a few nights
Christmas and New Year at hers, hotel otherwise
Mostly hotel, at hers for Christmas
questions.recommendation: Ask her outright and take the answer at face value. Then book the hotel nights in November, because London in December is not a city to leave to the last minute.

questions.question: Luggage transfer on the Camino, yes or no?
questions.why: For about €8 a stage a van takes your bag to the next guesthouse and you walk with a daypack. Purists carry everything. At 63, over six days, in Galician rain, carrying 8 kg is a genuinely different walk to carrying 3 kg.
options: Use it every day, walk light
Carry everything, that is the point
Book it and decide each morning
questions.recommendation: Use it. Nobody at the Pilgrim’s Office asks, the Compostela is the same, and you will enjoy the six days more. About €50 for the week.

questions.question: Do you want a scenic train day, or are the trains just transport?
questions.why: You said you like the idea of a proper train journey. There are two already inside this trip: Santiago to Sarria through Galicia, and the option of coming back from Santiago to Madrid on the high-speed line instead of flying. Neither is a hardship. The famous scenic ones in Britain, like Glasgow to Mallaig, are dark by four in January.
options: The trains already in the plan are enough
Add a day for one scenic line
Come home from Santiago via Madrid by train
questions.recommendation: Leave it. There is a lot in these five weeks already and the Camino is the part you will remember.
